name: JUNO — experimental hall and the Yangjiang and Taishan reactor buildings
notes: Baseline statements by the collaboration: "The detector is positioned near the first maximum of the solar-driven oscillations, at an optimized distance of 52.5 km, equidistant from all reactor cores of the Yangjiang and Taishan Nuclear Power Plants (NPP)" (arXiv:2511.14593, introduction); "the experimental site is at equal distances of ∼53 km from the Yangjiang NPP and the Taishan NPP" (arXiv:2104.02565, Sec. 1.2). The surveyed per-core baselines in Table 1 of arXiv:2104.02565 span 52.11 to 52.82 km, so the equal-distance figure is nominal. Checked 2026-10-25.

Core numbering YJ-1..6 / TS-1..2 is assigned by matching the order of the measured distances to the order of the published baselines; the OSM ways carry no unit numbers. The Taishan EPR units 3 and 4 (baselines 52.32 and 52.20 km in the CDR) were not built; arXiv:2104.02565 says only that two more cores 'possibly' may be built.
Far reactors: arXiv:2104.02565 Sec. 1.2 puts the Daya Bay complex 215 km (and Huizhou 265 km) from the detector, beyond a local map; Daya Bay has its own map (linked).

Residual: the six Yangjiang buildings are all 96-101 m farther from the published hall coordinate than the surveyed baselines say, the Taishan buildings agree to <= 16 m. The sign pattern is that of a ~100 m displacement of the published coordinate toward SSW, or of an OSM registration offset between the two plants; the sources cannot separate them.

summary.plain: The JUNO underground hall and the buildings of the two nuclear power plants whose antineutrinos it measures, to scale: six reactor buildings at Yangjiang and two at Taishan. The collaboration puts the detector 52.5 km from the reactor cores, and its surveyed distances to the individual cores run from 52.11 to 52.82 km. The map shows where the buildings stand; those baselines are checked against the drawn positions, but no baseline lines are drawn.
summary.technical: Published hall coordinate (arXiv:2104.02565, Sec. 1.2) and OSM reactor buildings of Yangjiang (six building=reactor ways) and Taishan (two nuclear-island buildings). Each building's centroid-to-hall distance is checked at 0.3 % tolerance against the GPS-surveyed core baselines of arXiv:2104.02565 Table 1 (YJ-1 to YJ-6: 52.74, 52.82, 52.41, 52.49, 52.11, 52.19 km; TS-1, TS-2: 52.77, 52.64 km; surveyed to 1 m). The JUNO Collaboration gives the nominal baseline as 52.5 km (arXiv:2511.14593, introduction) and as about 53 km (arXiv:2104.02565, Sec. 1.2). No baseline lines or distance labels are drawn. Companion to map:juno-jiangmen.
